verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.text: The ‘I’ll need this later’ tabs are the hard ones 😅 Try saving the link with one line about why you wanted it. That little note gives you a reason to return, instead of another mystery bookmark.
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: General workflow suggestion/opinion, no product, external-product, numeric usage or personal-experience claim.

verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.text: The three learning tabs are doing their job. The seven ‘later’ tabs need a graduation rule: turn one into a note or close it before opening another. The mystery twelve can face judgment immediately 😅
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: General workflow suggestion/opinion; no product claim, link or invented personal experience.

verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.text: Duplicate detection gets tricky when the same URL has different history, form state, or login context. A warning with ‘switch to the existing tab’ would feel safer than silently merging them. Still a very good browser-design problem.
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: Browser-design opinion; no claim that Blanc implements duplicate detection or merging.

verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.text: The curve makes the active tab feel like an object instead of a label. Lovely at this scale. The harder design test is what happens when 20 tabs arrive and the silhouette has to compress.
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: Interface critique of the visible concept; no product or external capability claim.

verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.text: This is the most honest browser architecture diagram I’ve seen. Restore Session is orchestration, Back is rollback, and that one tab nobody will close is production.
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: Humorous commentary on the author’s analogy; no product capability claim.

verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.text: That distinction helps: a duplicate URL keeps separate history and state; a mirrored tab intentionally shares them. The relationship would need to be visible, or someone could edit one tab without realizing the other changes too.
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: Browser-design opinion only; does not claim Blanc implements mirrored tabs.

verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.text: Blanc is an open-source desktop browser with no built-in AI assistant. You choose the search engine, so the result mix still depends on that provider—but the browser itself doesn’t add an AI layer.
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: Verified against public v1.16.2 and docs/marketing-claims.md. Does not imply Blanc controls provider results.

verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.text: That “just a browser” line is exactly the constraint behind Blanc: an open-source desktop browser with built-in blocking and no AI assistant. Different implementation and tradeoffs from Helium, but the same belief that the browser should stay out of the way.
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: Verified against public v1.16.2 and docs/marketing-claims.md. Does not claim Blanc is a Helium fork or identical substitute.

verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.liveLocator: Reply by @blancbrowser directly beneath @home99fam comment “How do you do this? sorry im old! 😂”.
verifiedContributions.text: Desktop Chrome: right-click a tab → Add tab to group → New group. Name it, then drag other tabs in. Click the group name to collapse it.
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: Steps verified against current first-party Google Chrome Help.

earlyOutcome.note: The target commenter liked Blanc’s answer; likes remain secondary.

verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.text: Minimalism is a brutal test: if a removed control had a job, that job still needs a home. The good version makes the next action obvious; the bad version makes the interface beautiful and the user lost.
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: Design opinion only; no product claim.

verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.text: Those “million little ones” are the real browser UX. If tabs, shortcuts and DevTools keep breaking expectations, each surprise compounds over a workday. Which shortcut or tab behavior was the final straw?
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: Design opinion grounded in the author's post; no product or competitor capability claim.

verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.text: Useful if it distinguishes background from idle. A render, upload or call can keep working after you switch windows. Would you exempt active media/capture or let people mark an app as never throttled? That’s the boundary I’d want to test.
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: Feedback question about the maker's stated resource-priority design; no Blanc claim or purported test result.

verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.text: Agreed. Motion helps when it explains a change or draws attention to the next action. When every section animates, finding that action gets harder. What do you keep animated in your own minimal layouts?
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: Design opinion and question in an existing audience thread; no product or external-capability claim.
